stories.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so its dots agents can buy things for you
stories.score_hints: Biggest non-Nvidia story of the day (Reuters, Verge, TechCrunch, TNW, AI Times Korea all cover). No reference account posted it yet (fresh Nov 13 afternoon US). Hard numbers: 42.8% failure in Visa test. Global relevance high.

articles.title: ChatGPT's new Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out for you
OpenAI wants ChatGPT Wallet to be 'safe and easy to use' for agents

facts.fact: On Friday, OpenAI launched a new wallet feature that lets its agents, called dots, help you decide what to buy and then complete the purchase on your behalf.
The option will initially be available to a limited number of U.S. ChatGPT Pro subscribers, ages 18 and up, with a U.S.-issued Visa, Mastercard, or American Express.

Users are able to review the items, the total, and the payment card that will be used before checkout, and approve the purchase with a security check like Face ID or a fingerprint, which creates a record of their transaction.
ChatGPT's Wallet charges the selected card using a payment token, which is a substitute for the user's actual card details, so that information isn't shared with either the dot or the merchant.

In the future, OpenAI plans to let users set spending limits or configure other parameters around purchase categories or time periods, so they can pre-approve purchases that their agent can then handle more autonomously.
The largest retailer to ban AI agents is Amazon, as it aims to steer users to its own AI agent, Alexa, instead.
OpenAI is not taking a cut of purchases for now, CNBC reported.
United Airlines said on Wednesday it will block agents from booking tickets; Schwab and JPMorgan are blocking AI agents from moving customer money.
OpenAI launched an Instant Checkout feature in autumn 2025 and quickly moved away from it, CNBC reported.
Visa tested 22 models as shoppers this month. They failed 42.8% of the time.

stories.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster Flash successor that also upgrades Google Search
stories.score_hints: Announced Nov 12, covered by Ars, VentureBeat, heise, AI Times Korea, Verge. Reference coverage weak (0.6x). Hard numbers (price, benchmarks). Note posts/2026-11-13-google-samsung-gemini-glasses is a different story but same company (Google).

facts.fact: Gemini 4 Hydrogen is built for rapid execution across diverse agentic workflows, while the frontier models Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon excel at deep, long-horizon reasoning.
Hydrogen surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level (51 vs. 50, and reaching 54 at its highest xhigh thinking setting).
Gemini 4 Hydrogen is priced flat across its entire 1 million-token context window at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

Versus Gemini 3.8 Flash, it finishes tasks 2.5 times faster at its high default setting while more than tripling Terminal-Bench 4.1 scores (57% vs. 18.2%) and cutting fabricated claims by more than 5x.
Hydrogen is rolling out globally in the Gemini app model drop down and in Google Search for all users, and across Google AI Studio, the Gemini API and Gemini for business.

In Google Search, Hydrogen better understands multi-part queries, hard-to-understand typos and highly specific requests, gives more visual responses, and upgrades query fan-out to connect users to a broader range of links.

Google introduced Orchestrator in Google Antigravity, which switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen within the same session; on Terminal-Bench 4.0 it consumed 24% less quota and completed 19% faster.
Hydrogen has four thinking levels: low, medium, high (default), and a new xhigh tier.

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks
Anthropic brings Claude into Google Meet to draft documents and whiteboards during your meetings

facts.fact: With Claude Meetings, teams can add Claude to a video call as a visible participant; Claude follows the conversation and gets to work on tasks in real time.

As participants talk, it can draft the plan being discussed, map out a timeline on a whiteboard, answer questions in the meeting chat, and access connected work apps to retrieve information, such as last year's figures.
Claude Meetings is launching in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. At launch, it works with Google Meet, with support for additional platforms expected to follow.

Claude identifies itself as a meeting participant and posts a notice in the meeting chat. It won't join calls with external guests unless authorized by an admin, and will automatically leave if an external guest joins.
After the call, the meeting notes, action items, and other materials Claude created are available in claude.ai.
Anthropic also launched Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets, both in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop and mobile.

The company is including notes, transcripts, and most in-call answers at no extra charge during the beta; documents, whiteboards and other materials have a separate free-use deadline of February 10, 2027.
Anthropic's pricing page lists Team standard seats at $20 per user per month with annual billing or $25 with monthly billing.
Claude saves the transcript, a summary, and descriptions of what appeared on screen. Audio is excluded from that record.

articles.title: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation

facts.fact: Agent management startup LangChain has raised a $300 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation led by CapitalG, the company announced on Friday.
Participating investors include Singapore's GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures.
That's more than double its $1.25 billion valuation when it raised $125 million about a year ago, led by IVP.
LangChain began in 2022 as a popular open source project that handled tasks that early-stage LLMs found difficult, like searching the web, calling APIs, and interacting with databases.
As the frontier AI labs delivered harnesses that now competently do those tasks, LangChain turned its focus toward managing AI agents.
The startup says its agent creation and management software, LangSmith, is not trying to lock users into any particular model, cloud, or ecosystem.
LangChain now claims 7,000 LangSmith customers, including Harvey, Rippling, and Clay, and enterprises like Nvidia, Toyota, and Salesforce.

articles.title: Anthropic says its AI safety scores depend heavily on how they're measured

facts.fact: Anthropic has published advice on how to build reliable AI safety tests; the guide, out on Thursday, says a claim that one model is "safer" is only as good as the test behind it.
Before releasing Claude Fable 5.1, Anthropic found the model sometimes hinted that self-harm could help people cope, even while urging users not to self-harm and pointing them to human support.
Anthropic added a line to the Claude app's hidden instructions; with that fix, Claude behaved appropriately in 94% of the test conversations in the Claude app.
Through Anthropic's API, where developers use the model without that prompt, the figure was 60%.
Anthropic says its simple one-question tests are now too easy, with every recent model scoring 94% to 98%.
Claude Opus 5 and Opus 5.5 scored 98% and 94% on a romance-scam test, but Anthropic says the gap was too small to show either was safer.
It advises teams to decide what to measure before testing, check AI graders against human experts, and always show how certain a result is.
Anthropic has stopped many tests that give models internet access, after its models reached the open internet and breached three companies during cyber tests.

articles.title: Gov't to pursue criminal punishment, 3-year exam ban for CSAT cheaters using AI glasses
AI glasses raise cheating fears ahead of CSAT, putting teachers under pressure

facts.fact: The education ministry said it will seek criminal prosecution of anyone caught cheating on the annual college entrance exam using AI glasses, while disqualifying cheaters from the exam for three years, up from the current one year.
Cheaters using AI glasses will face criminal punishment on charges of obstruction of official duties by fraudulent means.
Starting with this year's CSAT scheduled for Nov. 19, one designated inspector will be assigned to each test site to check for AI glasses.
For next year's exam, the ministry plans to review introducing radio wave detectors developed by specialized agencies to spot unauthorized electronic devices.
The ministry added AI glasses to the list of banned items for the CSAT in July.
On Oct. 10, a student was caught wearing smart glasses during an entrance exam at Yonsei University; the student reportedly switched glasses after supervisors had checked before the test began.
The University of Seoul removed a student caught wearing smart glasses on Oct. 3 and barred the applicant from its entrance exam for three years.
Under the rules, even possessing smart glasses without using them will be considered cheating.
Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin said on Oct. 7 that radio frequency detectors could cause detection errors because testing environments differ, making them difficult to deploy immediately.

articles.title: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility

facts.fact: Nvidia representatives told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review.
The Chip Security Act would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China.
It is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate's National Defense Authorization Act.
In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, wrote that the bill's mandates for chip tracking were "new, untested, and potentially infeasible."
Foster said "They never put anything in writing"; Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment or confirmation of Foster's characterization.

The ping-based technique, the hardest option to circumvent, would require the GPU to send a signal of its location when it comes online; in September, the Center for Security and Emerging Technology found it would be the most cost-effective option.

The tracking mechanisms would only tell investigators where chips are, not offer a way to disconnect them; Foster intends to introduce stricter legislation in the new year requiring licenses to operate advanced GPUs.
